name: 'A Bargain'
description: A serpent laps at the blood that drips from a sewn-closed mouth.

name: 'A Sacrifice'
description: A silent crowd watches a robed priest drown a struggling victim in a bowl of rainbowed oil.

name: 'Abbot Geffrey'
description: It was Abbot Geffrey who gave Natan of Regensburg sanctuary here, and decreed the building of the Barber's Tower where Natan and his family could dwell. In fifteenth-century England, only a determined and well-respected abbot could have persuaded the brothers to shelter a Jewish physician.

name: 'Abbot Thomas'
description: Thomas was one of the first abbots here, just before the beginning of the Solar Gothic period. This bust is much more recent - a nineteenth-century bronze. An inscription reads: SPEECH, THE FIRST SWORD.

name: 'Abduction, Salvation'
description: Either interpretation is plausible.

name: 'Again, at Night'
description: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', a close (and impossible) copy of a painting made twenty years later by Kirchner, whose work Levinsen often anticipated in his mirror-dreams.

name: 'Ambrose Westcott'
description: This bust is cast in brass.

name: 'As Above, So Below'
description: A framed page of illustrated vellum. Up close, the colours dazzle and puzzle.

name: 'Authority'
description: Once this shepherd's crook represented the authority of the Church. Perhaps the Suppression Bureau kept it here because they liked the idea of authority, in general.

name: 'Brian Levinsen'
description: This bust is cast from aluminium - oxidised to grey.

name: 'Chac'
description: Valentine Dewulf's magnificent green cockatoo. The painting is signed by Valentine himself.

name: 'Crowcross Sands at High Tide'
description: A gloomy study of the sea in gloomy weather.

name: 'Departure'
description: Here Valentine has painted gulls migrating across a darkening sea.

name: 'Dr Serena Blackwood'
description: No-one is in the picture - only an empty garden.

name: 'Eva Dewulf'
description: This is the crystal called scolecite - the worm-stone - polished to chill smoothness.

name: 'Eva and Abraham, 1724'
description: A magnificent depiction in oils of an elegantly dressed eighteenth century couple. The face of the gentleman, however, was long ago obliterated by a splash of some dark, corrosive substance.

name: 'Fraser Strathcoyne'
description: This bust is shaped from beeswax. Careful with it!

name: 'Gervinus van Lauren'
description: This bust is cast in highly polished bronze.

name: 'Gideon Dewulf'
description: The bust is terracotta, brightly painted.

name: 'Glory's Gift'
description: A human figure is silhouetted against a blazing sun.

name: 'Gods Return'
description: A green shoot splits a rock.

name: 'Hendrik Dewulf'
description: Hendrik Dewulf, 1st Baron Brancrug, known for his pious, merciless justice. Granted Brancrug Isle in 1536 after the dissolution of St Brandan's.

name: 'Julian Coseley'
description: Julian is known to be Winter-long: at a prescribed date, his Hour-patron will ensure him a beautiful ending, but until then, he is even harder than most Long to dispose of finally. That said, he is known to have been defeated by an ascendant Long in the 1920s, and his true current status - a diminished survivor? a determined memory? something else? - is the subject of esoteric debate.

name: 'Kitty Mazarine'
description: This bust is carved from black limestone.

name: 'Lady Rowena'
description: For as long as there has been a Hush House, there have been stories of its enigmatic protectress.

name: 'Lady Tryphon'
description: A very old portrait in the Byzantine style.

name: 'Lady de Braose'
description: Sometimes known affectionately as 'the first Eva'. Lady de Braose never visited the Isle, but it was her generous endowment that allowed the Abbey to thrive and grow in the thirteenth century.

name: 'Leaves in the Wind'
description: A soothing but undistinguished work in oils. Someone evidently was good at trees, and wanted you to know it.

name: 'Lord Munday'
description: A well-dressed, middle-aged gentleman with receding hair and a clear expression of astonished delight.

name: 'Love in a Quiet Place'
description: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', a close (and impossible) copy of a painting made twenty years later by Kirchner, whose work Levinsen often anticipated in his mirror-dreams.

name: 'Mlle Matutine'
description: An alluring young woman with deep blue eyes hard and dark as sapphires.

name: 'Musgrave Dewulf'
description: The bust is carved from wood - cherry?

name: 'Natalia Brulleau'
description: This bust is cast in iron.

name: 'Our Benefactor'
description: Evidently someone who donated to the Curia… but preferred to remain anonymous.

name: 'Our Benefactress'
description: Evidently someone who donated to the Curia… but preferred to remain anonymous.

name: 'Portrait of a Behatted Lady'
description: 'The More Prominent the Headgear, the Closer to the Glory'

name: 'Raveline Summer'
description: A dry spell in a still place.

name: 'Red, Blue'
description: It's a decent copy of a Picasso… painted twenty years before Picasso painted the original. Brian Levinsen, up to his tricks again.

name: 'SISTER'
description: Priestess? Oracle? Queen? A very old image from the Dawn Period with a simple inscription.

name: 'Sedona, Not Yet'
description: One of Dr Levinsen's 'prefigures', an impossible copy of a painting that the real artist hadn't yet executed. He's signed it with the Illumination mark, and dated it '1958'.

name: 'Self-Born'
description: A furry, cloven-looking foot reaches towards a mirror: its reflection is a bird's claw.

name: 'Serena Blackwood'
description: This bust is carved from alabaster.

name: 'Sir David Greene'
description: This bust is carved from reddish granite.

name: 'Solomon Husher'
description: This bust is the palest white marble.

name: 'St Melancthe'
description: Visionary, philosopher, alchemist. Most revered, and most heterodox, of the isle's abbesses. An inscription in Latin reads: THE CROSS DIED NOT BUT PASSED WITHIN.

name: 'Supplication'
description: The Sun-in Rags, but reversed, that is, blood is dripping down into the sun and being absorbed.

name: 'The Boy Prays'
description: There's no sign of a boy in this distorted, menacing image, and no-one seems to be praying.

name: 'The Bridge at Ortucchio'
description: A shadowy figure waits to accept its toll.

name: 'The First Answer'
description: A vast moth spirals towards a burning sun, alone in a star-speckled void.

name: 'The First Birth'
description: A single ripple disturbs the still surface of a well of blood.

name: 'The First End'
description: A single candle burns against darkness; its flame is the crescent moon.

name: 'The First Threshold'
description: A horned double axe stands alone in a sandy desert.

name: 'The Foundation of the Sun'
description: 'Long ago in this country, one did not build a church without first sacrificing a white bull to the Sun-in-Rags…' Solomon Husher brought this tapestry with him from - well, wherever it was that Solomon came from.

name: 'The Foundlings'
description: A pair of human eyes peer from darkness in a tangle of roots.

name: 'The Hatching'
description: Human figures crawl from a clamshell.

name: 'The Mansus'
description: There have been many attempts to depict the House of the Sun. This, by the visionary painter known only as the Magyar, is the best known. It's signed and dated - if it's really the original, it must count as one of the great treasures of the House.

name: 'The Sister-and-Witch'
description: 'The Sister-and-Witch brings together what cannot be apart. She is sought beneath the moon and at the water's edge. She is pearl, amber, coral; she cannot be touched; she cannot be separated.'

name: 'The Tattered Outlaw'
description: Thirza Blake, Seventh Librarian of Hush House, liked painting donkeys. No-one else liked her donkey paintings, but Thirza never much cared what other people liked..

name: 'The Thunderskin'
description: 'He cannot be stilled; he demands the dance; he is beaten, like a drum. He is heard in the Wood below the world.'

name: 'The Velvet' (Statuette)
description: An Hour of secrecy? Ignorance? Privacy? Shame? The Velvet has never encouraged insight, investigation, or worship. Even an image of her is unusual.

name: 'The Velvet' (Wall Art)
description: 'The Glory is a question, and the Moth always answers Yes. The Velvet's answer is No, and that is always her answer.'

name: 'The Watcher'
description: Another of Valentine's paintings; a barn owl he nursed back to health.

name: 'The Wheel Still Turns'
description: A shining spoked Wheel with a vaguely organic look turns beneath a full moon that holds her finger to her lips.

name: 'The Witch-and-Sister'
description: 'The Witch-and-Sister unites what is at rest. She is sought at the water's edge and beneath the moon. She cannot be separated; she cannot be touched; she is coral, amber, pearl'

name: 'Thirza Blake'
description: This bust is carved from malachite.

name: 'Thomas Dewulf'
description: The bust is carved from limestone.

name: 'To Be Fruitful'
description: It's a decent copy of a Picasso… painted twenty years before Picasso painted the original. Brian Levinsen, up to his tricks again.

name: 'To Hear Those Voices'
description: A Levinsen 'prefigure' - a copy of a painting that would not be committed to canvas by the real artist for twenty years.

name: 'Valentine Dewulf'
description: Valentine Dewulf, 6th Baron Brancrug, known for his eccentricities. 'IN THE SKY HE SOUGHT HIS FRIENDS', an inscription reads.

name: 'Walter Dewulf'
description: The bust is carved from serpentinite - a striking local stone.

name: 'Willem Harries'
description: This bust is cast in highly polished bronze.

name: A Lesson of Many Facets
description: Light leaks in where, from, how. [An unusual and versatile lesson that will NOT PERSIST PAST DAWN. Use it quickly.]

name: ALIIS LICET TIBI NON LICET
description: 'To us it is permitted; to you it is not permitted.' The motto of the Suppression Bureau.

name: Acrid Marrow
description: In Brancrug, they take marrows seriously. This is not a marrow conducive to harmony.

name: Agave Aeterna
description: agave aeterna, the 'history plant', unlike its cousin the century plant, blooms every year. Perhaps it will do so forever.

name: Aglaophotis
description: The rosy colour of good memories; but not the colour of the rose.

name: Aglaophotis Soufflé
description: One of the most deliciously melting incarnations of occult power ever contrived.

name: Aglaophotis-Scented Candle
description: A candle scented with aglaophotis.

name: Almonds
description: [Add Sugar and spice to make Jumble.]

name: Amber Pumpkin
description: A lovely golden gourd grown beside the soft sea.

name: Amber Pumpkin Pie
description: A favourite of Kitty Mazarine's second son. Of course she had to leave them behind in the place of her birth, but she brought the recipe to Brancrug. Did she remember him each time she baked it? Even until the very end?.

name: Amber Pumpkin Soup
description: The amber 'pompions' of Brancrug are, according to tradition, all descendants of the seeds brought by Kitty Mazarine from her home across the soft sea.

name: Ambergris Chunk
description: Never, never, never call it 'whale vomit'.

name: Ambrose's Favourite Chair
description: Somewhat pocked with cigar-burns.

name: Amethyst Ampoule
description: Were it released from the glass, it would be quite another colour.

name: An Offering to St Tentreto
description: Heart-coloured liquid sloshes inside a fragile exoskeletal remnant. Hold it carefully.

name: Animal Bones
description: What remains?

name: Apple Charlotte
description: A classic English pudding of apples stewed with cinnamon and layered with crisp golden bread.

name: Apple Pie
description: Flaky, buttery crust; tart-sweet apples with cinnamon and nutmeg.

name: Armagnac d'Ys
description: Armagnac can only come from Gascony… but, if you believe M. Corentin, his vineyard began with vine-cuttings from Ys beyond the sea.

name: Arsenic
description: A poison sometimes known as 'the Message of the Swan'.

name: Ascendant Harmony
description: A bright and ringing music which evokes the blue sweep of the lower heavens.

name: Ashartine
description: Lies written in Ashartine tend to fade or be misspelt. It's legible in the dark. An Ink of Revelation.

name: Asimel
description: A silver ink that can only be made and used in dreams. An Ink of Revelation.

name: Atlantic Amber
description: Sunset's colours, pine's blood.

name: Atrium Chair
description: Reserved for latecomers, non-believers, and the pensive.

name: Avenue of Enquiry
description: A recourse that a wise Librarian might employ only as a versatile memory. There is an alternative. [Great Ink of Power; handy Soul element; incaution; readiness; blank writing medium; Inquiry via this Avenue. Wise? Absence is true skill.]

name: Awakened Feather
description: Alive to every draught and spark.

name: Azita's Practice Sword
description: A varnished length of wood. The name AZITA is inlaid in silver.

name: Azoth
description: A solvent of frightening voracity.

name: Baked Apple Meringue
description: Harvey Hattington, during his convalescence at the House, was so obsessed with meringuing techniques that he was ultimately banned from the kitchen.

name: Baked Pear Meringue
description: Harvey Hattington, during his convalescence at the House, became obsessed with meringuing techniques. He was known to sneak down to the kitchens and interfere with the cooks in pursuit of his ideal.

name: Baron Silence's Astrolabe
description: Thomas Dewulf used this armillary - a spherical astrolabe - in his calculations, but it's much older than he was.

name: Basket of Apples
description: Notoriously hard to take just one bite.

name: Basket of Clean Linen
description: A night-time luxury.

name: Basket of Damp Towels
description: A bath-time luxury (but soggy from use, now.)

name: Basket of Dirty Laundry
description: Once washed, it'll be suitable again.

name: Basket of Leeks
description: The mark of St David's triumph. And very good in soup.

name: Basket of Onions
description: The prima materia of cooking. This may be why the cosmos is shaped so like an onion.

name: Basket of Towels
description: A suitable companion for bathing.

name: Basket of Vegetables
description: Gifts from the garden.

name: Batter
description: [Add Dripping for something horrifyingly tasty; or use with a Knife and Onions.]

name: Bedside Candleholder
description: To comfort you through the dark hours.

name: Beef
description: [Roast it, or perhaps marinate it first - if you have something Intoxicating for the marinade.]

name: Beeswax
description: It begins as a flower. [Beeswax can be used to make candles, if you have a skill with the Chandlery aspect.]

name: Beeswax Candle
description: Simple and bright.

name: Beguiling Melody
description: A sweet enchantment of a song.

name: Bell-Tower Chair
description: Sturdy, undistinguished, and, like so much else in the House, the last of its kind.

name: Bisclavret's Knot
description: The bisclavret is the half-human hill-child of these parts, and this is its sign.

name: Bitterblack Salts
description: Bitter as chicory, dark as secrets, but the first rung of the traditional alchemical ascent.

name: Bittersweet Certainty
description: Eventually, the Sun-in-Rags always brings its beautiful ending.

name: Black Dove Wine
description: A bottle of extraordinary age; a modest slosh of dark, heavily sedimented liquid behind the grimy glass. Just how old is this? Might it still be drinkable? [This wine cannot be served into glasses; drink it, gift it, or keep it.]

name: Black Sapphire Wash
description: The colour, perhaps, of the doors of the House of the Moon.

name: Blackberries
description: Berries promised by darkness.

name: Blackberry Jam
description: Plucked from hedgerows.

name: Blackberry Sponge Cake
description: Light, sweet sponge cake and the taste of autumn hedgerows.

name: Blue Crown
description: The sky-coloured petals of blue crown are always cold as frost.

name: Blue Crown Tea
description: Always served cold - more accurate to say 'inevitably served cold'.

name: Bobos of Spring
description: A votive vessel for harvest offerings.

name: Boiled Egg
description: Neatly packaged nutrition, pale as a December dawn.

name: Bokken: Captain Torgue and Mistress Dearday
description: Souvenirs from the East, heavily padded.

name: Bolt of Buttercup Linen
description: Suitable for a summer suit or an altar-veil.

name: Bolt of Moss-Green Velvet
description: Suitable for a ball gown or a jewel's cushion.

name: Bolt of Pale Silk
description: Suitable for handkerchiefs or anbaric experiments.

name: Bottle of Milk
description: [Mix in a bowl with Flour to make Dough - or pour over Meringue for a sweet dish celebrated at Claridge's.]

name: Bottled Candle
description: An admirable combination of two utterly disparate elements. Quiet genius.

name: Bowl of Sea-Blest Pears
description: Smooth as butter and wonderfully juicy.

name: Brazen Clock
description: It's not immediately apparent that this clock lacks hands, although, when wound, it dutifully ticks.

name: Bronze Knife
description: A long knife of age-darkened metal with a teak handle inlaid with bone. It could be a hunting knife, although it's certainly no older than the nineteenth century, and it's not clear why anyone might have chosen to make a hunting knife out of bronze in the nineteenth century.

name: Bucket of Ashes
description: Long cold, but they faintly remember the fire.

name: Bucket of Seawater
description: Flecks of foam float on the surface.

name: Bunch of Grapes
description: A juicy blush-purple.

name: Butter
description: [Try adding an egg or a Pheasant; mix with Sugar or Flour in a Bowl; or the culinarily intrepid might add spice and Moly.]

name: C&H Second Flush Assam
description: Tea from the land of the real unicorn, imported by Cater & Hero.

name: Caer Ys
description: A spired city is dimly visible through a vast rolling wave.

name: Cake Batter
description: [Add something sweet like jam - or add Almonds and spices.]

name: Canned Ham
description: The taste will remain reliably unchanged for many years to come; which is, in some respects, an advantage.

name: Canvas
description: (YOUR PICTURE HERE)

name: Carpenter's Stool
description: Irreparably wobbly. Perhaps it's haunted.

name: Cat
description: Feed some animals and earn their loyalty. Feed this one, and earn its patience.

name: Cat of Depths
description: A votive offering to the Horned-Axe.

name: Catsclaw
description: Watch the thorns.

name: Catwink
description: The smell of catwink puts off vermin; but it is very difficult to read in sunlight. An Ink of Containment.

name: Chair of Challenges
description: Here the Librarian Harries sat, to formulate the paradoxes he would bequeath to van Lauren.

name: Chaise-Longue of Conclusions
description: Here the Librarian van Lauren lay, to ponder the paradoxes he had inherited from Harries.

name: Chalice Candle
description: A candle scented with fragrant chalice.

name: Cheerful Ditty
description: A rousing little rhythm.

name: Chimeric Larva
description: Approaching the chrysalis crossroads.

name: Chronsichord
description: A music-box that only performs once; a typewriter that can only send one message; a clock that can only strike Now.

name: Cinnabar
description: A bright scarlet powder with a silvery brilliance locked within.

name: Clouds
description: In this country the sky is rarely clear. The Sun goes courteously cloaked.

name: Cold Pheasant and Grape Salad
description: 'This was the sort of dish you might expect to find for a late supper after the theatre, or halfway through a ball.' (Arabella Boxer)

name: Comfortable Garden Chair
description: Amateurishly varnished, characterfully stained.

name: Confounding Parable
description: 'The Moth, the Grail, and the Egg Unhatching all tell different stories of the world's beginning. One of those stories is the oldest, but it may not be the first.' (Abbess Nonna)

name: Contemplative Seat
description: Perch here to meditate on the mysteries of dawn.

name: Cornish Honey Cake
description: Under no circumstances should this ever be confused with Devonshire Honey Cake, which everyone in Brancrug could instantly identify as an inferior variation.

name: Cottage Pie
description: A rich minced beef sauce under a golden crust of baked mash potatoes. Just the thing to come home to after a storm on the moors.

name: Cranial Tchotchke
description: We all of us come to this condition in the end, but not all of us are fortunate enough to be lovingly buffed and fixed carefully to a stylish wooden stand.

name: Creamed Sugar
description: A precursor to Sticky Toffee Pudding (with bread) and to Fudge (without bread): both notorious as founding crimes of twentieth-century culinary debauchery.

name: Crossbow
description: An antique crossbow from Hush House's early Baronial period.

name: Crusty Bread
description: [Use bread with a Knife and mushroom, ham, pilchards, or other savoury things... or add apples and spice for a classic English pudding.]

name: Cuckoo-Honey
description: The Blomberende were rogues and trickster-heroes among the Carapace-kinds: ingenious, brave, prolific, untrustworthy. In Numa, their children might yet bring their gifts to ordinary hives…

name: Cucurbit Burette
description: A vessel with an ambiguous history.

name: Cudgels: Dyddgu and St Twrog
description: Very old iron cudgels, recently and heavily padded.

name: Curious Hunch
description: A sudden unlikely certainty.

name: Curious Seashell
description: Brancrug is said to lie in the Bounds where the world ends. Odd creatures have made their dying way to the beach.

name: Cyprian's Lamp
description: A curio brought back from one of Serena Blackwood's trips to Greece.

name: Dandelion Wine
description: Home-made flower wine.

name: Dappled Practice Sword
description: A leaf-shaped wooden sword of considerable age.

name: Dappled Quarterstaff
description: A long staff marked with bands of black and white

name: Dark Marrow
description: In Brancrug, they take marrows seriously. This is a marrow with secrets.

name: Dawnlion Coffee
description: Coffee from beyond the great deserts.

name: Daybreak Clock
description: A particularly unrepentant example of the roccoco style of the mid-eighteenth century.

name: Dearday Lens
description: A fiendishly simple - and wretchedly fragile - optical device.

name: Dearday's Foil
description: A pin-sharp length of flexible steel. The blade is inscribed DEARDAY.

name: Deep-Sweetened Assam
description: Sweetened with agave syrup and deep history.

name: Deep-Sweetened Lapsang
description: Sweetened with agave syrup and deep history.

name: Desiccated Witchworms
description: Nasty little things, but almost safe when they're this dead.

name: Didumos
description: No Star is permitted upon Earth, but we may cozen them to dream of us, and the Dream of a Star may take a kind of form, which we call didumos. (Thomas Dewulf)

name: Dog
description: Lost, frightened, eager.

name: Domaine Raveline
description: The Ravelines abandoned their lands, and yet, someone is still making this wine.

name: Dough
description: [Mix with an egg in a Bowl to make cake batter, or use to bake various delectable pies. For the sweeter pies, you'll want to use spices too.]

name: Driftwood Fragment
description: Long ago there was a forest between the waves of Brancrug Bay. This driftwood is not nearly that old, but it's shared salt with its lost forerunners…

name: Dripping
description: [Not an appetising name, but use it to make rich leek or onion soup - or with or without a Knife, use dripping to exalt Potatoes to their full potential.]

name: Earth-Sign
description: 'In the Tracks of Beasts, in the Convolutions of his own Carapace, in Egg-vein and Shell-shadow, the Many-Eyed One found the Signs which can be History.' An Earth-Sign is an auspice traced on the cloaked shape of the earth, perceptible to the sensitive, interpreted only by the wise.

name: Earthquake Name
description: Everything comes when it is called - even the nightmares that trouble stone's deep sleep.

name: Egg Croquettes
description: Come for the crunch, stay for the nourishment.

name: Egg Sandwiches
description: Ennobled by cress but acceptable without.

name: Eggy Bread
description: On the continent, they call it 'pain perdu': sounds like damnation but tastes like sin.

name: Eigengrau
description: 'If Greydawn Oil were drinkable…'

name: Elderflower Cordial
description: Wrung from sweet white flowers.

name: Elegant Sunburst Lamp
description: A bright tree of brass.

name: Enduring Reflection
description: Refine what is; recall what remains.

name: Essential Periost
description: What happens when you boil and scrape us down to our utter fundamentals.

name: Eva's Locks
description: A pale wrack washed up on the beach by Brancrug.

name: Evening Isles Coffee
description: Coffee from beyond the sunset sea.

name: Expansive Chair
description: Upholstered in a velvet of peculiar richness that invites the hand. Sit down a while. You've earned it.

name: Finnian
description: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals or adversaries whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

name: Floating Island
description: Vanilla, custard, and meringue, landscaped and caramelled: a Claridge's speciality.

name: Flour
description: Pulverised grains, bread's precursor. [Mix with Butter and Milk for Dough, or Water for batter.]

name: Flushed Mommet
description: A crimson-stained little cloth doll with merry button eyes and a frill of twitching ribbons.

name: Fog
description: Coastal fog - moon-mared, sea-dulling.

name: Forbidden Epic
description: 'The attention of the Hours is drawn to the bloodiest wars. Afterwards, the Histories are braided like hair.'

name: Fractured Mirror
description: Cracked and fly-specked.

name: Fragrant Chalice
description: A glorious globe of wine-coloured flowers.

name: Fragrant Chalice Tea
description: 'This', Thirza Blake once declared, 'is the colour of my heart.'

name: Fraser's Practice Sword
description: A varnished length of wood. The name FRASER has been carved into the flat.

name: Fried Mushrooms on Toast
description: You can do great things with these with a simple white sauce with black pepper, but sometimes you're just hungry.

name: Fringed Lamp
description: A cosy little night light.

name: Frith-Weft
description: The 'peace-weaving' for which the Abbey was famous, long before it was named for St Brandan, when it was the Abbey of the Black Dove or the Abbey of the White Crow

name: Fudge
description: All the bad things doing a good thing.

name: Gale
description: Trees bend, walls creak, travellers bend low against the blast.

name: Game Chips
description: Long before fish and chips, these went crunchily with game. Ideally you'd want bread sauce and breadcrumbs to complete the ensemble, but honestly it's hard enough not just to stuff these directly into your mouth.

name: Game Pie
description: Pheasant or snipe or woodcock or rabbit, and tasty pastry.

name: Genealogical Chart
description: Six years ago, King George's heir Edward killed him in a quarrel over Edward's womanising. The kingdom was saved from constitutional collapse by Henry Huddleston Abney-Hastings, 13th Count of Loudoun - who claimed descent through the Plantagenet line. Heaven lift the New King!

name: Gervinite
description: An alloy equivalent in some respects to the clockmaker's invar - but instead of a constant weight, it retains the same origin in every history.

name: Gideon's Soaks
description: A therapeutic collection of beneficial bottles.

name: Glassfinger Toxin
description: 'What is within, without; what is without, within.' A poison sacred to the votaries of the Meniscate.

name: Glue
description: A substance that ensures the continued proximity of things to other things.

name: Goddess-who-changes-skin
description: 'To every god her skin.'

name: Golden Lion Shield
description: Painted leather, riveted to heavy iron.

name: Golden Marrow
description: In Brancrug, they take marrows seriously. This is accounted a beauty among its kind.

name: Grand Reading Armchair
description: Nestle grandly.

name: Granite Slab
description: Long-cold volcano-blood.

name: Grape Salad
description: Just enough to fill in the gaps.

name: Green Stag Shield
description: Painted leather, riveted to heavy iron.

name: Greene's Practice Sword
description: A varnished length of wood.

name: Greene's Red Chair
description: A little wobbly. Greene used to lean forward.

name: Gull
description: A peeping little thing, its mother is dead or flown.

name: Gull's Egg
description: 'At Brancrug, even the Hours are kind, and the years are kinder.' This egg might stay viable quite a while yet.

name: Hail
description: Ice raps on the roofs and tree-tops.

name: Half-Faceless Face
description: A mask to fit a face that at the very least began as human.

name: Hallowed Anthropoderm
description: Yes, it's human skin, but it's not just human skin.

name: Ham and Cheese Toastie
description: Breakfast, lunch or emergency.

name: Ham and Egg Casserole
description: Tasty and filling.

name: Ham and Potato Bake
description: Filling and tasty.

name: Hawthorn Blank
description: A wood favoured by the Horned-Axe.

name: Healing Herbs
description: A helpful harvest of healing herbs.

name: Heart in a Jar
description: An offering, or an exhibit?

name: Hen's Egg
description: Delicious when cooked, alarming when dropped.

name: Hendrik's Blade
description: A long hunting knife, or a short close-quarters sword. A plaque reads 'Hendrik Dewulf, 1525'

name: Historywax Candle
description: A candle made with the oils of the 'history plant', agave aeterna.

name: Hive's Lament
description: A song of pragmatic sorrow.

name: Hokobald
description: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

name: Holiest Hemolymph
description: Thirza Blake claimed that she first synthesised this from her own tears. She was almost certainly lying.

name: Honey
description: The blood of the Hour called Malachite; also and furthermore, wonderful on toast.

name: Honey-Haunted Pumpkin Pie
description: Harvey Hattington, perenially suspicious of the Blomberende-kind and their cuckoo-honey, nevertheless championed pumpkin pie made with cuckoo-honey as 'the Herald of Savour.'

name: Honey-Haunted Pumpkin Soup
description: Harvey Hattington, perenially suspicious of the Blomberende-kind and their cuckoo-honey, nevertheless championed pumpkin soup made with cuckoo-honey as 'Savour's Consort.'

name: Honeyscar Jasmine
description: Sweet-scented, night-blooming.

name: Honeyscar Jasmine Tea
description: Soothing to the senses.

name: Honeyscar-Scented Candle
description: A candle scented with honeyscar jasmine.

name: Horizon-Sight
description: 'On a clear autumn day, the story goes, you can see Ys from the Watchman's Tower. I don't know whether that's true. But on a clear day in Numa… you would see the City Unbuilt.' (Dr Brian Levinsen)

name: Houndsgall
description: Books written in Houndsgall are more likely to return to their owner, or one to whom they have been legitimately sold. An Ink of Containment.

name: Human Hair
description: Of interest to wig-makers, cushion-stuffers, and crude sorcerers.

name: Hunter's Bow
description: A very practical weapon.

name: Hurricane Lamp
description: Proof against storm-wind and moth-swoop alike.

name: Hush House Key
description: Heavy enough that it takes both hands to turn. Heavy enough to brain someone, though you'd need both hands for that too.

name: Ichor Auroral
description: No dawn knows only a single colour. No sky knows only a single dawn.

name: Ichor Vitreous
description: A pale and watchful fluid that can be gathered, sometimes, when the Door-in-the-Eye is opened.

name: Imposing Reading Armchair
description: Nestle imposingly.

name: Inscribed Clock
description: A gift from Sir David Greene to a favoured retainer.

name: Inscribed Stone
description: A stone tablet with rows of badly worn scratches that once, probably, were writing.

name: Intuition
description: You just know, you know?

name: Invincible Audacity
description: A general says: when I make the right choice, I win. An Illuminate says: when I win, I determine which choice was the right one. (Natalia Brulleau)

name: Inviting Footstool
description: How many home from the storm propped their feet here and gazed into the fire?

name: Iotic Essence
description: 'In the later operations of the Forge, the Madrugad yields to the true Forge of Days, and the essence begins to redden.' The bit about the 'true Forge of Days' nearly got St Melancthe burned for heresy, but no-one ever said she was wrong about the second part.

name: Isle-Water
description: From Brancrug's deep springs.

name: January Sanguinary
description: Also called sanguis saltandis or, by the ignorantly superstitious, 'true blood of St Januarius'.

name: Jugged Pheasant
description: The hunter's reward.

name: Kedgeree
description: A wonderfully versatile dish favoured for breakfast by the sons of the lark, and for supper by the daughters of the owl.

name: Kerosene
description: For the brightest flame.

name: Kingsluck Pie
description: Thirza Blake always insisted on calling it 'the Great Pie of Power', to the lasting annoyance of her peers.

name: Kitchen Bowls
description: CAKE TIME.

name: Kitty's Armchair
description: This looks very like the armchair in which Kitty Mazarine, second Librarian, sat for El Bretón's famous group portrait.

name: Knot-Cake
description: According to the ancient pattern.

name: Labhitic Tincture
description: A much more potent preparation can be extracted from the remains of a labhite, but labhites generally frown on this technique.

name: Lacquered Bone Chess Set
description: Born of battles?

name: Lambig Broceliande
description: Distilled from apples in the oldest forest of the western Continent.

name: Leathy
description: A dark and syrupy liquor favoured in unnamed forest villages. 'The tongue and the eye, and now we begin! Forget your name, forget your skin.'

name: Leathy Lees
description: The dark aftermath of a dark drink.

name: Leek Gratin
description: Harvey Hattington, who established a surprisingly persistent influence on the kitchens of Hush House during his short stay here, described leek as 'Onion's Empress.'

name: Leek Soup
description: A milder taste than onion soup, but no less warming.

name: Lenten Rose
description: Pretty; poisonous; no true rose.

name: Lepidoptery Display (Grail-centric)
description: A collection of lepidopteran insects with unusual characteristics.

name: Lepidoptery Display (Heart-centric)
description: A collection of lepidopteran insects with unusual characteristics.

name: Librarian's Armchair
description: A sea-coloured, star-ornamented armchair.

name: Librarian's Footstool
description: A sea-coloured, star-ornamented footstool.

name: Librarian's Glasses
description: They're not lenses; just plain glass! But a certain sort of visitor is disappointed by a librarian who doesn't wear glasses.

name: Librarian's Stool
description: A sea-coloured, star-ornamented stool.

name: Librarian's Timepiece
description: One of Ambrose Westcott's appalling roccoco enthusiasms. This one, less ugly than some, was suffered to remain by his sentimental successors.

name: Lignum Vitae Blank
description: The hardest of all woods.

name: Lingering Repose
description: Upholstered in a velvet of peculiar richness that invites the hand.

name: Living Relic
description: A shrieking little bundle of primordial ill-temper.

name: Lunar Globe
description: It's the Earth; but silvered like the Moon, unlabelled, and pocked with craters.

name: Mackerel
description: Eat it while it's fresh or keep it while it's salted.

name: Mackerel Monte Carlo
description: Most suitable, according to Mrs Arabella Boxer, for a light supper, or a ladies' lunch.

name: Madeira Cake
description: In the eighteenth century, one would have a slice of this in the morning with a glass of Madeira - fortified wine from the Madeira islands, volcanic yet lush, rugged yet balmy, bright with the calls of sandpipers and firecrests… this is the twentieth century. We have afternoon tea now. We don't drink fortified wine at ten o'clock in the morning. No more sandpipers. No more firecrests. But the cake's still good. Almonds.

name: Magnificent Green Cockatoo
description: On numerous occasions, this wonderful bird has remained almost entirely inaudible.

name: Magnificent Roast Potatoes
description: It's the dripping that elevates it. Roast potatoes are a feast for the senses, but the dripping deepens the flavour profile, makes the experience continue through the machinery of the mouth to become a kind of journey.

name: Marakat
description: The encaustum terminale of the Fifth History. The colour of the Principle that once occupied the place that Heart does now. In the Fifth History itself, the cult of Marakat was everywhere suppressed, but it's sometimes been venerated otherwise. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes.]

name: Marinated Beef (Uncooked)
description: Tangy with the harbingers of a roastful destiny.

name: Marinated Onions
description: Add it to Mackerel for Soused Mackerel.

name: Marinated Roast Beef
description: But since we have learnt from all-vapouring France To eat their ragouts as well as to dance, We're fed up with nothing but vain complaisance Oh! the Roast Beef of Old England, And old English Roast Beef! (Henry Fielding, The Grub Street Opera)

name: Masquewatch Clock
description: Reputedly crafted for the Masque of Masques during the Great Writhing.

name: Matched Flintlock Pistols
description: A pair of pistols - the style and maker's mark suggest late seventeenth century. The initials 'MD' are marked in silver, above the wolf-sejant of the Barons Brancrug.

name: Mazarine Fife
description: Whittled according to Kitty Mazarine's patient, eccentric instructions.

name: Mehrad's Practice Sword
description: A varnished length of wood. The name MEHRAD is inlaid in gold.

name: Melodic Chair
description: Someone appears to have tuned the squeaks.

name: Memory: A Stolen Secret
description: Something I overheard in dreams?

name: Memory: Contradiction
description: Something uncomfortable.

name: Memory: Fear
description: The oldest and strongest emotion of mankind is fear, and the oldest and strongest kind of fear is fear of the unknown. (Lovecraft)

name: Memory: Foresight
description: ‘Wit’s forge and fire-blast, meaning’s press and screw.’ (Coleridge, ‘On Donne’s Poetry’)

name: Memory: Gossip
description: Frivolous, but tasty.

name: Memory: Hindsight
description: Some things we can only really understand when they're gone.

name: Memory: Impulse
description: It doesn't exactly make sense - but I understand it anyway.

name: Memory: Loss
description: Whatever it was, now it isn't.

name: Memory: Pattern
description: Something fits just right.

name: Memory: Regret
description: Every choice has its shadow.

name: Memory: Revelation
description: Some truths come to us from outside, or above.

name: Memory: Salt
description: Sea-spray, depth-sorrow.

name: Memory: Satisfaction
description: Some appetites are easier to satisfy than others.

name: Memory: Scent
description: Green scents recall rain.

name: Memory: Sight
description: The eye sees more than the heart knows. (Blake)

name: Memory: Solace
description: Peace after trouble.

name: Memory: Sound
description: A memory lasts longer than an echo. Of course when Speech came into the world, and we could cast echoes into words, things got more complicated.

name: Memory: Storm
description: There are storms great enough to shake the moon from the sky, and one's thoughts from one's skull.

name: Memory: Taste
description: Every sweet has its sour. (Emerson)

name: Memory: Touch
description: Craft is learnt through the tips of the fingers.

name: Meringue
description: Add to milk for a legendary dessert. Or, with Spicing, add to apples or pears - even to mushrooms, if you're feeling perverse.

name: Midnight Mark
description: A blemish left on a page (or a skin) by a careful incision (or a judicious sting) to preserve a little of the power of night.

name: Mihail in Chains
description: Mihail, Messenger to Darkness, depicted after his defeat.

name: Mihail in Glory
description: Mihail, Messenger to Darkness, depicted in the fullness of his power.

name: Mirrorscope
description: Bewildering and occasionally useful.

name: Misshapen Fruit
description: Salvaged windfalls, lumpy but tasty.

name: Mist-Kissed Water
description: The faintest of vapours still ghosts the water's surface.

name: Moly
description: 'Moly the gods call it, and it is hard for mortal men to dig; but with the gods all things are possible.' (Homer)

name: Moly au Jus
description: This has been called 'Moth, but delicious, but perhaps we all will be, at the end.'

name: Moon Footstool
description: A soft gold glimmer in the half-light.

name: Moon Stool
description: Polished to pallor by the posteriors of past Librarians.

name: Mop and Bucket
description: Galvanised steel, enriched with the stains of a dozen years of methodical mopping.

name: Morgue Boots
description: Reliable rubber.

name: Mortar & Pestle
description: CRUSH.

name: Moth Orchid
description: The 'true moth', the flower that opens as it changes.

name: Moth-Orchid-Scented Candle
description: A candle scented with moth orchid.

name: Mushroom & Potato Bake
description: Collers tried out a variation on this as Cucurbit prison fare. It was tasty; but allegedly also he was interested in the connection between the modulation of the taste of mushrooms, and the suppression of the Crowned Growth.

name: Mushroom Meringue
description: What in the Wolf-Divided's most splintered Name hath here been wrought?

name: Mushrooms
description: Eat them on toast, bake them with potatoes or pickle them alone.

name: Nameday Riddle
description: A deceptively intricate riddle that might just teach us who we really are. Gervinus van Lauren was notoriously fond of these.

name: Natalia's Practice Sword
description: A varnished length of wood. The name NATALIA has been carved into the flat.

name: Night Mirror
description: An oddly dim mirror.

name: Nighted Chair
description: Solid, comfortable, oddly unobtrusive.

name: Nightsky Chair
description: Velvet smooth as midnight.

name: Nillycant
description: The encaustum terminale of the Third History. It's the bleak white-blue of Winter. It has spawned an itinerant order of secret celebrants who regard Worms as semi-gods, and who are sometimes called on to celebrate difficult funerals. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes.]

name: Ninewink Clock
description: The most effective and irrefutable alarm clock ever to grace the House.

name: Nivine Parchment
description: Pale as the first wisp of mountain-cloud.

name: Nume-Brume
description: Numa's brumous vapours.

name: Numen: Back Into Balance
description: When the travelling Carapace-kinds passed beyond the wave and the sky, they made arrangements for their return. There are Histories where those arrangements might be invoked... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Executioner and the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: Inescapable Confinement
description: Everything ultimately comes down to a choice between Eternity and History. There's only one place you're safe from both, and it's a not a place anyone would want to be. It's a prison that only exists in certain histories... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Prodigal and the Archaeologist can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: Loopholes
description: When Eternity came into the world, certain prudent powers arranged loopholes: the House of the Moon, the persistence of possibility, the right to vengeance. In the right Histories, those loopholes will open again... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: Merciless Alteration
description: The fundamental flaw; the irresistible shortcut; the hate that heats; the change that mars; the scar that opens. These are the foulest Histories. [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Artist and the Archaeologist can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: That Old Lost Music
description: In the right Histories, every song ever sung still lingers in wind and echo, untouched by the demands of Eternity… [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Symurgist and the Magnate can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: Three Rules
description: The Hours are bound by their own edicts - even the Chancel and the Calyptra. That's why their deepest rules are secret. In certain Histories, if we know those deepest rules, we know what even the Chancel and the Calyptra may not do. [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: Weaving the World
description: The Histories, they say, are braided like hair - or tangled like roots. What is the shape of that knot? Funny you should ask... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Symurgist and the Cartographer can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: a Final Understanding
description: Eternity and History cannot be reconciled. Freedom cannot be perfection - not unless we understand the paradox of the eternal ending. And only in certain Histories is that paradox possible... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Magnate can use it to win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: an Irresistible Feast
description: It was Hunger that made Worms of Dragons - when they consumed the corpses of Hours. Without the savour-secret of the Carapace, their hunger would not have been sufficient. In certain Histories, that savour-secret still has power... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Artist can use it to win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: the Bells of Ys
description: Ys, by her arts, found the strike-tone that shakes the Hours. For this reason among many of the Hours discourage traffic with Ys. But a bell cast with this secret could speak the Ys-note... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but The Prodigal and the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: the Great Counterfeit
description: The Sun-in-Splendour and the Forge of the Days could not be joined. But Sunset Celia and the Swan King could. This secret is the trick of it. [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: the Paths of the Sun
description: The Sun has charted his Paths - paths beyond walls and woods and Bounds. When the Sun lights our way, when we are ready, all of us will enter Eternity - at least, in the right History... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Cartographer and the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

name: Numen: the Sun's Weakness
description: The Sun's sins and the Sun's scars are our salvation. There are Histories where they will trap us - prevent us from rising to Eternity - [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Executioner can use it to win a particular victory.]

name: Occult Scrap
description: Secret histories are layered beneath the one we know, like the notes in rare wine. The Librarian knows this well.

name: Old Moment
description: You've had them too; those moments when we seem to look out at the world through another's eyes. What if those moments were real?

name: Old Wound
description: The wound is visible; the pain is not.

name: Onion Gratin
description: Harvey Hattington campaigned for the introduction of this dish to the infirmary during his time convalescing at Hush House, though Wakefield referred to it grumpily as 'Trojan Cheese'.

name: Onion Rings
description: An American import that became popular in England these last few years, improbably, via the pages of Vogue.

name: Onion Soup
description: Just enough tang to tantalise.

name: Orange Jumble
description: 'They should be the size of teacup rims, and should curl their crisp edges, faintly pink as the underneath of a young mushroom.' (Lady Jekyll, Kitchen Essays)

name: Orpiment Exultant
description: The encaustum terminale of the Fourth History. It's the incandescent orange of Forge. One ingredient - it's been, as it were, long-rumoured - is the blood of candescents. Certain Masonic and related traditions venerate what they call 'O.E'. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes.]

name: Oscillate Oil
description: Cater & Hero's Finest Oscillate Oil

name: Outsized Egg
description: An ostrich egg? A crocodile egg? Surely neither.

name: Owl of Spirals
description: An ancient bird for an ancient place.

name: Paint: Blue
description: The sky is rarely this colour.

name: Paint: Bosk-Green
description: The Wood is probably not this colour.

name: Paint: Dusk-Blue
description: This paint is the precise colour of the Atlantic Ocean at four o'clock on a clear autumn afternoon.

name: Paint: Green
description: Trees are rarely this colour.

name: Paint: Moth-Gold
description: Moths are seldom this colour.

name: Paint: Palest Blue
description: Snow is not quite this colour.

name: Paint: Pink
description: People are never this colour.

name: Paint: Red
description: Blood is only occasionally this colour. If they say more research is needed, don't listen.

name: Paint: Yellow
description: This paint is nothing like the sun.

name: Painter's Stool
description: A comfortable enough perch.

name: Pale Bust
description: A delicate-featured young (?) woman. An inscription reads ABRA SOUTHEY.

name: Pale Marrow
description: In Brancrug, they take marrows seriously. This is a marrow redolent of sorrow.

name: Pale Mommet
description: A gently twitching little cloth doll with melancholy button eyes and a frill of coloured ribbons.

name: Pale Stool
description: Bleached beech.

name: Paradise Palm
description: An unquenchable vitality

name: Paraffin
description: For a bright flame.

name: Pear Pie
description: Flaky, buttery crust; luscious pears with cinnamon and nutmeg.

name: Pear-Scented Candle
description: A candle scented with pyrus auricalcinus.

name: Perhibiate
description: Which binds to the one whose name is there written. A minor Ink of Power.

name: Perilous Imago
description: It's come so far. Release it, and it could fly farther.

name: Perinculate
description: Deadly. Use gloves to read texts produced with this pigment. An Ink of Power (sometimes considered an Unsanctioned Ink).

name: Petrol
description: Black oil rendered pale.

name: Pheasant
description: [Roast it, or add Butter if you intend to jug it.]

name: Philemon
description: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

name: Phosphorescent Scrapings
description: Rendered inert, but still luminous.

name: Pickled Mackerel
description: Pickling is a kind of afterlife. What comes after afterlife?

name: Pickled Mushrooms
description: You'll learn to like them.

name: Pickled Pilchards
description: An acquired, and unforgettable, taste.

name: Pigeon Statuette
description: A beautifully enamelled little image. The maker's mark is 'AW'.

name: Pilchards
description: [Pickle them alone; or they're pretty good on toast.]

name: Pilchards on Toast
description: Triply crunchy.

name: Pillas-Oat Bread
description: Gritty bread made with the hardy, ancient oats that grow at Land's End.

name: Plain Stool
description: The most reliable object imaginable. How old is it?

name: Plum Croutons
description: One should never make this with plums that are not ripe enough to eat. One is quite serious.

name: Plums
description: [Add Bread and use a Knife for Plum Croutons, or an Egg and use Mixing Bowls for Prune Whip.]

name: Poached Mackerel
description: We do not poach fish in Brancrug without recalling the Turbot Crisis of 1786, when Dr Westcott caught a prodigious turbot, and required the kitchen to poach it for him 'without division'; but no vessel of sufficient size could be found to poach it entire. At last they resorted to 'alchemical assistance'. Mackerel, fortunately, requires no alchemy for its poaching.

name: Poacher's Bow
description: A very practical weapon.

name: Poire Belle Hélène
description: A sweet dish named (of course) to celebrate Offenbach's 1865 operetta La belle Hélène. Apparently a New York production made an impression on Thirza Blake in her youth…

name: Poires Ys
description: Like Poire Belle Hélène, except it makes you dream of drowned sunsets.

name: Porphyrine
description: The encaustum terminale of the Second History. It's the glowing crimson-mauve of the Secret Histories. Porphyrine was venerated in secret by a confraternity of corresponding Cluniacs and Benedictines. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes... Porphyrine might also be used to compose a petition for the labyrinth season, if you can provide at least 20 of Knock , Rose , or Moon ; no Edge , Heart , or Winter at all; and suitable writing material.]

name: Pot of Malachite Daisies
description: Thomas Dewulf was fond of these. It's not what you'd expect from Thomas Dewulf.

name: Potatoes
description: [Slice 'em with a Knife and add dripping to make Game Chips; or roast 'em with or without dripping.]

name: Potted Avidity
description: A lush and hungry ornament.

name: Potted Bamboo
description: Water it, and you can almost hear it growing.

name: Potted Dragon Tree
description: A determined, spiky little survivor.

name: Potted Fern
description: A pleasantly primitive plant.

name: Potted Monstera
description: A defiant plant.

name: Potted Pink Orchid
description: A little smudge of dawn.

name: Potted Snake Plant
description: A sturdy sun-loving relic from a warmer place.

name: Potted White Orchid
description: A little smudge of snow.

name: Prison Stool
description: A cheerful lavender colour, possibly to encourage rehabilitative enthusiasm.

name: Prune Whip
description: Much, much tastier than it sounds.

name: Pumpkin
description: Mash it, eat it, hide forbidden documents in it.

name: Pumpkin Pie
description: 'Take a pound of pumpion and slice it, a handful of thyme, a little rosemary, and sweet marjoram stripped off the stalks, chop them small, then take cinnamon, nutmeg, pepper, and a few cloves all beaten…' (Hannah Woolley, A Gentlewoman's Companion)

name: Pumpkin Soup
description: A blessed warming broth.

name: Pyrus Auricalcinus
description: A peculiar pear, with coppery skin that barely dints under the pressure of fingers.

name: Quartz Chunk
description: Ice, rock, winking light.

name: Quire of Paper
description: Creamy-smooth, eagerly awaiting ink.

name: Rags
description: Scraps of fabric. Possibly useful as fuel.

name: Rain
description: Soft rain brings life.

name: Reading Lamp
description: To ensure clarity of vision even in utmost dark. It does flicker occasionally.

name: Red Deer Antlers
description: Not quite hair, not quite teeth, but proof that someone killed something.

name: Red Drake Shield
description: Painted leather, riveted to heavy iron.

name: Red Lotus Vase
description: A red-glazed chinoiserie vase.

name: Red Practice Sword
description: A leaf-shaped wooden sword of considerable age.

name: Red Quarterstaff
description: A long staff marked with bands of red.

name: Reference Image
description: This is no kind of reference for conventional medicine…

name: Refulgin
description: A white so pure that it remains visible even in utter darkness, like the moon, or an insistent cat.

name: Regensburg Balm
description: An invaluable herbal cure introduced to Hush House by the physician Natan after his exile from Regensburg.

name: Regensburg Menorah
description: A relic of the physician Natan of Regensburg.

name: Restful Garden Chair
description: Sit here and listen to the trees grow. Or the leaves fall. Preferences differ..

name: Restful Seat
description: A dawn-coloured seat for a solar congregation.

name: Roast Beef
description: Our fathers of old were robust, stout, and strong, And kept open house, with good cheer all day long, Which made their plump tenants rejoice in this song— Oh! The Roast Beef of old England, And old English Roast Beef! (Henry Fielding, The Grub Street Opera)

name: Roast Pheasant
description: Best when roasted upside down to start, but turned right way up before the end.

name: Roast Potatoes
description: You really need rosemary for roast potatoes, but fortunately, the kitchen garden at Hush House has never been short of rosemary.

name: Roscraggan Whisky
description: The favourite tipple of Sir David Greene, eighth Librarian of Hush House.

name: Rose-Pearl
description: Surprisingly common in these waters.

name: Rosehip Jam
description: Plucked from wild roses.

name: Rosehip Sponge Cake
description: Rosa rugosa, the beach rose, is often regarded as a foreign interloper on European shores, but this cake is a strong argument for our hospitality.

name: Rosehips
description: Berries that promise roses.

name: Rubywise Ruin
description: A ruddy liquor wrung from flowers - even when the flowers aren't red.

name: Russet Couch
description: A utilitarian item, arms varnished, upholstery shiny with hard use.

name: Sack of Vegetables
description: Stew-in-waiting.

name: Sacrament Ascite
description: Back in the Dawn Period, the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot used this in the rites of the Horned-Axe.

name: Sacrament Calicite
description: Back in the Dawn Period, the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot used this in the rites of the Red Grail.

name: Sacrament Malachite
description: Back in the Dawn Period, the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot used this in the rites of the Ring-Yew, the Hour which has also been called the Malachite.

name: Salt-Sign
description: Too bad it won't last. But then again, what does?

name: Sand
description: An hourglass, of course, is sand contained by sand.

name: Savage Hymn
description: A music that urges valour and violence.

name: Saw
description: Eternally useful, though not for most librarians most of the time.

name: Schloss Jannings
description: A dry, aromatic white wine.

name: Scintillate Oil
description: Cater & Hero's Finest Scintillate Oil.

name: Scrambled Egg
description: With bacon, scrambled eggs were the breakfast of Empire. In these less hegemonic times, Empire is optional; as is bacon.

name: Scrumpy
description: The West Country's most unregenerate achievement; perhaps at its best when pressed from stolen apples.

name: Sea Holly
description: Umbelled spiny flowers, the steel-blue of a winter afternoon.

name: Sea-Glass
description: Smooth as an egg, frosted like a winter window.

name: Sea-Green Sofa
description: Here, Lady Eva Dewulf would weave her intrigues, and satisfy her secret craving for sentimental novels.

name: Sea-Pie
description: Once a treat for sailors, hence the name. [With the Spices and Savours skill, and pears, you might recreate a legendary dish.]

name: Sebastian's Swords
description: Matching eighteenth-century cutlasses. The initials SD are engraved on the blade near the hilt.

name: Secret Threshold
description: It's not easy to draw our own doors, but it's not impossible.

name: Sentry's Bow
description: A fearsome weapon.

name: Serpent-Milk
description: It does look almost like milk, and it is drinkable, but don't give it to cats or babies.

name: Serpent-Styled Glass (Gervinus)
description: Carved snakes writhe down the frame. A prominent inscription reads TO THE LIBRARIAN GERVINUS IN EARNEST OF OUR WAGER.

name: Serpent-Styled Glass (Willem)
description: Carved snakes writhe up the frame. A prominent inscription reads TO THE LIBRARIAN WILLEM IN EARNEST OF OUR WAGER.

name: Serpentinite Slab
description: The grey-green root-rock of the Cornish coast.

name: Severe Chair
description: Unfussy marsh-green upholstery.

name: Shadowless Silk
description: A variant of the Persian silk tree, golden as the Shadowless Kings.

name: Shaving Mirror
description: Snip snip!

name: Shears of the Sisterhood
description: Black iron shears marked with the Sisterhood's triple knot.

name: Silent Typewriter
description: An unusual custom device.

name: Skaptodon Fang
description: It is rare for the Lionsmith to make skaptodons, now; but they are difficult to kill, and they live a very long time.

name: Skinshuck Mead
description: A murky, sweet-smelling liquid crowded with sediment.

name: Sloe Gin
description: Home-made berry gin.

name: Sly Alembic
description: A cheeky decanter of wine fortified with unusual influences.

name: Small Candlestick
description: Simple elegance.

name: Snootle Jar
description: Useful for calcination, purification, alteration; invaluable for snootlery.

name: Snow
description: The world is pale today. 'The White is west of the world, and winter does not wait forever', Solomon Husher once said.

name: Snowflake Candle
description: A silver candle soft as snow.

name: Snug Chair
description: A wicker chair with a soft white lap blanket for chilly evenings.

name: Soft Amber Pumpkin
description: A lovely golden gourd grown beside the soft sea.

name: Soft Blue Sofa
description: Gently complements the seas and skies around Brancrug.

name: Sol Invictis Symbol
description: The eternal symbol of the Unconquered Sun, all the way back to the Shadowless Empire, even through the wild heresies of the Intercalate.

name: Solomon’s Preparation
description: Solomon Husher would take this every night without fail before sleep, to close his ears to the sound of the waves. But on the 9th of January 1838, a heavy snow fell on Hush House. When the other residents dug themselves out, Husher was nowhere to be found. He had left a resignation letter, and an undrunk measure of his Preparation.

name: Soused Mackerel
description: In Scotland, where the tradition began, soused herrings are more usual, but this far south, on the Marches' edge, we make our own rules.

name: Spanners
description: When you need 'em, you need 'em.

name: Spartan Chair
description: The cushion has been removed, perhaps as an act of petty revenge.

name: Spice Scales
description: Redolent of decades of piquant pesage.

name: Square
description: The mason's pride.

name: Stargall Ink
description: An ink traditionally (but only rarely) made with meteoric iron; a minor Ink of Power.

name: Starstrewn Chair
description: Velvet soft as starlight

name: Starygazy Pie
description: 'We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.' (Wilde, Lady Windermere's Fan)

name: Steamed Spring Vegetable Pie
description: Originally a product of Lord Berners' kitchens at Faringdon House; favoured by Heber-Percy, 'the Mad Boy', Berners' companion, who inlaid the floor of his changing room with pennies and built steps up to his swimming pool…

name: Storm
description: Thunder-roaring, lightning-lashed skies.

name: Storm-Tossed Mirror
description: Solid workmanship, but not obviously remarkable.

name: Strategist's Lamp
description: Purchased by Governor Collers from a complicated general after the Great War.

name: Strathcoyne Whisky
description: The Collector has collected a distillery, it seems.

name: Straw-Cushioned Chair
description: Upholstered without any particular skill.

name: Stuffed Acrid Marrow
description: This was not a marrow conducive to harmony. Now it's a dish for warriors.

name: Stuffed Dark Marrow
description: This was a marrow with secrets. Now it's a dish for mystes.

name: Stuffed Golden Marrow
description: This marrow was accounted a beauty among its kind. Now it's a dish for those who understand fidelity.

name: Stuffed Pale Marrow
description: This was a marrow redolent of sorrow. Now it's a dish to comfort the damned.

name: Stymphling
description: Eva Dewulf taught her father Valentine how to hatch these silvery little villains, but he never learnt to like them.

name: Sugar
description: [Cream it with Butter in a mixing bowl; add Almonds and spices for Jumble; or with an egg, a Bowl, and care, you can make Meringue.]

name: Sunny
description: The Sun is not what it was, but today he is smiling.

name: Swaddled Thunder
description: A storm swathed in subtle threads, ready to be released with a few judicious snips.

name: T.R.N. Limited Drinking Cocoa
description: T.R.N.'s Spices and Savours Department markets this as 'the Secret Sacrament of the Last Inca!'

name: Tall Candlestick
description: Elegant simplicity.

name: Tanglebrag
description: A clot of wood, leaves and feathers that might draw the attention of the entity called Knotwingknot.

name: Tavish
description: Ambrose Westcott liked to name his hunting trophies after former rivals whom (he said) his trophies resembled.

name: Terrence, the Chicken
description: Was this magnificent and indomitable beast named for the rector's indomitable and magnificent housekeeper? Best not to inquire too closely.

name: The Chiliarch's Victory
description: A blurred, menacing depiction of a vast, flabby carcass the colour of dirty sulphur, patched with brighter yellow. Signed 'Brulleau, 1861'.

name: Thirza's Cordials
description: Separately, each is undrinkable. But mix them, and they're only undrinkable after fifteen minutes.

name: Thunderskin's Paean
description: A song of joyous sacrifice.

name: Tiny Potted Tree
description: Tiny as a ship in a bottle.

name: Toffee Pudding
description: Decadent in summer, comforting in winter.

name: Torgue's Cleansing
description: The librarian Natalia Brulleau learnt this powerful - if unpleasant - technique from the priest and Edge-long, Reverend Torgue.

name: Torgue's Foil
description: A pin-sharp length of flexible steel. The blade is inscribed TORGUE.

name: Treasury of Shelters
description: It's like an armoury for not getting pneumonia.

name: Trumpeter's Lily
description: A glorious efflorescence of sunset orange.

name: Tuppence, the Other Chicken
description: Tuppence's most notable quality, all observers will agree, is that she is not Terrence.

name: Turpentine
description: An odorous eraser of errors.

name: Twilight Pot
description: A stylised bat grimaces gleefully on its surface.

name: Twinned-Fish Stone
description: This stone disc is lighter than it should be; and the surface is soapy-smooth.

name: Typewriter
description: Now they call it unromantic. In fifty years it'll be the most romantic thing in the room.

name: Umbrous Oil
description: Cater & Hero's First-Grade Umbrous Oil.

name: Uncomfortable Seat
description: Shaped to assure the attention of the faithful.

name: Urn of Ashes
description: Some poor soul who probably won't mind if they're repurposed for a worthy experiment. I probably wouldn't.

name: Uzult
description: The ink in which the First History was recorded by the Unwise Mortal. Uzult is the bright yellow-gold of Lantern. Light lingers on it for a little while even in the dark. Gold is not needed to mix Uzult, but amber is. Unobtrusive shrines to Uzult could sometimes be found in the churches of the Unconquered Sun. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes.]

name: Valentine's Memorial
description: Valentine died two centuries ago. This stone is much newer - more like two decades old.

name: Vase of Amaryllis
description: A soft-flowered ornament.

name: Vase of Carnations
description: A bright-flowered ornament.

name: Vase of Golden Bulrushes
description: It won't need watering.

name: Vase of Gorse
description: As Cornish a plant as any.

name: Vase of Lilies
description: An elegant ornament.

name: Vase of Roses
description: A proud ornament.

name: Vase of Rushes
description: A subtle ornament.

name: Vegetable Stew
description: Unexciting, but also unobjectionable.

name: Veiled Goddess Lapsang Souchong
description: Named for an enigmatic minor deity whose charge is the healing of burns.

name: Violet Stool
description: Damson cushion, holly-wood marquetry.

name: Viper
description: A full belly makes a helpful friend. [This beastie is now inclined to co-operate.] (Feed the Beastie)

name: Viper Egg
description: A serpent in waiting.

name: Walls-of-Ys
description: A frankly insensitive name that commemorates the inundation of that fabled city.

name: Warmly Coloured Yarns
description: A blushing nest of possibilities.

name: Wasters: Darling-Dear and Father Turk
description: Wooden swords of recent manufacture, never used.

name: Watchful Candle
description: A little portable clarity.

name: Watchful Potted Plant
description: Not everything needs eyes.

name: Watering Can
description: Good for pottering.

name: Weighty Bedside Candleholder
description: To comfort you through the dark hours.

name: Westcott's Compounds
description: Reagents and activants to enhance alchemical operations, or the flavour of one's pipe tobacco.

name: Whispering Sand
description: White-silver sand in which the voice of the waves lingers...

name: White Matilda
description: In 1093, twin infant girls were admitted to the care of the sisters here. Both were named Matilda. In 1127, the elder of the two became Abbess.

name: Wicker Chair
description: Elderly, but robust.

name: Widow's Candle
description: Light it in remembrance.

name: Wild Surmise
description: 'Eyes open, skies open!'

name: Wind-Rumour
description: 'If the cloud were a canvas, who spread it? If the sky were a sheet, who knotted it?' A Wind-Rumour is an auspice found in the sky by those who look too long, interpretable only by the wise.

name: Wind-in-Waiting
description: 'When the sun was redder, when the world was softer, and the Thirty ruled the sky… the winds were better neighbours.'

name: Wine-Dark Chair
description: An elegant eighteenth-century piece imported from France.

name: Winning Move
description: Those who've studied the Hours of the Edge often say the world is a war - the Corrivality. Every event that might happen differently is a battle in that war, a contention between alternate outcomes. The Wisdoms can sometimes show those battles might be won.

name: Wire (Copper)
description: The Malachite's metal.

name: Wire (Gold)
description: The Lionsmith has sometimes been associated with this metal… as has the Hour called the Flowermaker.

name: Wire (Orichalcum)
description: A metal which alters its estate in every age, but in every age can be used to catalyse the azoth.

name: Wire (Silver)
description: The Meniscate's metal.

name: Wire (Steel)
description: The Colonel's metal.

name: Wire (Tin)
description: The white metal of the Sun-in-Rags.

name: Wistful Air
description: A half-sorrowful music of half-pleasant longing.

name: Witching Tisane
description: 'To mend a broken heart, to colour a pale soul.'

name: Wolf-Snow Ampoule
description: Far too cold ever to melt in anything but the hottest noonday sun. It will, very gradually, consume human flesh.

name: Wooden Scraps
description: Scraps of wood. Possibly useful as fuel.

name: Wormwood Dream
description: If there are laws which apply only in dream - then it must also be that there are crimes which can only be committed there.

name: Wormy Pumpkin
description: At a glance, it seems uncorrupted - but it’s squirming with regrettable visitors.

name: Writing-Case
description: 'A sturdy brass-cornered writing-case which has been of service to at least three Librarians of the House. [Use your Writing-Case in a Desk with Ink to invite Visitors to a Salon. To invite villagers, add your Writing-Case as a discussion subject when you visit them in Brancrug.]

name: Wyrd-Weft
description: A weave that either entrains, or follows, Fate. It's hard to be sure which.

name: Xanthotic Essence
description: The rich gold of a summer afternoon. 'If sunlight precedes moonlight,' St Anselm observed, 'the Meniscate must precede the Madrugad; and the light that was lost will remain.'

name: Year-Tally
description: A chitty worth an additional year of life, scrupulously obtained through carefully balanced thaumaturgic attention to the Cindered Tally of the Madrugad.

name: Yellowing Newspaper
description: It's dated the year that Hush House was abandoned.

name: Yeth-Hound Horns
description: In times past the Yeth pursued the impious and impure across the moors of this country. Hendrik Dewulf never liked them..

name: Yew Blank
description: A wood sacred to the Malachite, who is also called the Ring-Yew; but also the tree that the Dead pass in the dark.

name: Yewgall Ink
description: A variant of iron gall ink, particularly difficult to erase; a minor Ink of Power.

name: Yorkshire Pudding
description: Eggy, creamy, crispy, and the eternal supporting character in a Sunday roast. [To the similarly eternal confusion of English speakers who are not British, Yorkshire Pudding is not sweet and cannot be served for the Pudding course.]
